title: Bring the local viewer up to the reviewed mockup interaction surface

needs: The local viewer must retain the interaction surfaces agreed in the reviewed mockup, not merely its visual theme.
An operator must be able to find a report, compare its states, read linked runbooks and discover commands without the viewer ever executing one.
Viewer regressions need a real-browser check over generated fixture reports; static source assertions alone cannot prove interaction or layout.
context: The current viewer already renders the report DAG, detail panel, runbook links, first-run guidance and an in-place image wipe.
The mockup additionally specifies command menus, Chain/Compare/Runbooks workspaces, an outliner filter, a report-section rail, a labelled comparison handle and a richer first-run splash.
The viewer remains a plain local page: it reads report files, has no framework or build requirement, and must never start an operation.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The viewer exposes Chain, Compare and Runbooks workspaces; each is keyboard-accessible and preserves the selected report where applicable.
AC2: Menus and visible actions show copyable CLI commands but never execute an operation, open an engine or mutate work/.
AC3: The outliner filters operation and runbook rows by visible text without changing the underlying report chain.
AC4: The comparison view labels both states, exposes a visible divider, and supports pointer drag plus keyboard range adjustment through a native control.
AC5: First run presents the available starter commands, recent-chain absence, doctor results and platform-specific fixes without any blank panel.
AC6: A repeatable Chrome smoke test opens the generated fixture, exercises workspace, filter and wipe interactions, and captures screenshots outside the repository.

product.title: Reviewable local viewer interaction parity
product.overview: Completes the reviewed local viewer interface around the existing report-driven core. It adds discoverable navigation and command guidance while preserving the hard boundary that the page reads and the CLI acts.
goals: Make the mockup's high-value review paths real and keyboard-accessible.
Keep every action informational or copyable rather than executable from the browser.
Verify the real page in Chrome against generated reports before accepting layout or interaction changes.
non_goals: A browser-to-engine execution bridge, local privileged server or job queue.
A framework, bundler, dependency or hosted UI service.
Pixel-identical rendering across operating systems and fonts.
A 3D viewport or editing geometry from the viewer.

backlog_items.title: Add safe workspace navigation and command discovery to the viewer
problem: The current page implements the Chain surface only, although the reviewed mockup makes comparison and runbooks first-class workspaces.
The current page has no menus that teach the CLI commands available to the operator.
scope_in: Chain, Compare and Runbooks tabs using the current static page and report payload.
Accessible menus that reveal commands as text and use no execution endpoint or browser-side mutation.
Selection and focus behavior shared by the three workspaces.
scope_out: Running commands, clipboard permissions, opening Blender, or adding a server API.
Replacing the report-driven graph or details panel.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Each workspace can be selected by mouse and keyboard and reports remain readable after changing workspace.
AC2: Every menu action displays its CLI command and no action invokes fetch, a process, or a write operation.

backlog_items.title: Complete the mockup review controls without weakening the local page boundary
problem: Finding a report in a longer chain and moving among report sections still requires manual scrolling.
The in-place wipe lacks the mockup's explicit state labels and visible affordance.
The first-run page is informative but omits the reviewed starter and recent-chain structure.
scope_in: A local outliner filter, report-section rail, labelled native comparison control and first-run panels driven by existing doctor and report data.
No-report and no-comparison states with explicit guidance.
scope_out: Persisting UI preferences or introducing a database.
Inventing a command when a manifest does not expose one.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Filtering is reversible and hides only nonmatching visible rows.
AC2: The comparison divider remains draggable and keyboard-adjustable while before/after labels identify the two states.
AC3: First run describes a valid next command and every displayed environment state has an explanation.

backlog_items.title: Exercise the viewer in a real browser against the generated fixture
problem: Host self-checks inspect payloads and source invariants but do not prove browser layout, tab changes, filtering or drag behavior.
The reviewed mockup and current viewer had never been captured at the same viewport for an explicit parity audit.
scope_in: A small repeatable Chrome smoke script that builds the fixture page, opens it at a fixed viewport, interacts with the defined controls and writes screenshots to a temporary directory.
Assertions on observable DOM state and native range values; screenshots are review artefacts, not committed golden images.
scope_out: A cross-platform pixel-diff suite or committed screenshots.
A new browser-test framework when Chrome and platform tooling already provide the needed smoke path.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: One command produces a fixture-page screenshot and fails when Chrome cannot load the page.
AC2: The smoke test verifies a tab change, a filtered row set and a changed native wipe value.
AC3: The test leaves no generated browser artefact tracked by Git.

orchestration_task.title: Deliver reviewed viewer interaction parity
plan: Define the browser smoke contract against the current generated fixture before changing the viewer.
Add safe workspace navigation and command-only menus without creating an execution path.
Add filter, report navigation, labelled comparison and first-run refinements with the existing plain JavaScript and CSS.
Run fixture, browser smoke, type checks and workflow validation; record screenshots outside the repository.
